Well hi. I was a Plex user for a while but I lost interest into it. Help me understand what's exciting about it these days?

When's the last time that you have used it?

Here are the biggest things about it that get me so pumped up

  • I can share my library with anybody, or access my library from outside of the network

  • How easy and seamless it is to start watching something on one device and then move to another device

  • The organization of the files and the metadata that it grabs, the fact that I just have a folder with files that only have the movie titles and then plex takes that and grabs posters, descriptions, ratings, and all of that good stuff and presents it in a way that looks good is pretty amazing

It's been maybe a year. I guess i just had a lot of trouble organizing my content. I was constantly having things not get indexed right in the library. I even tried some software I can't remember the name of to auto rename files and such but it was always a hassle and there were some things I never got quite right.

Ah, I had that same problem initially when it would recognize the files but it didn't grab the metadata properly, I had to manually hit refresh for each title for it to actually grab the data.

Luckily they ended up fixing that about two weeks after I had gotten into it I think.

http://imgur.com/MyDjN2O as you can see, I didn't really do anything special when naming the files, just had to put the movie titles in there.

http://imgur.com/U0GskO9 Another great thing about it is the filters that you can use to narrow down what you'd like to watch that day.

There's a lot of solutions these days for grabbing content and automatically manicuring the file names.

NZBget, Deluge, Sonarr, CouchPotato, filebot, and makeMKV

Can be a headache to get them all setup correctly, but when they're humming along it's a beautiful thing.
